title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : "Sulyvahn" is phonetically similar to the Irish name "Súileabháin" (related to the more common, Anglicized name "Sullivan") which means "One-eyed" in English. It can also mean "little dark-eyed one" in Irish, which matches the black rings he gives to his knights to devolve them.
**Both names are ironic, given that he lacks eyes.
In Japanese, Sulyvahn's title is written like 法王. This word is used to denote Buddha, and also the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope Pope] - the highest dignitary in Catholic Church. Although the word pontiff technically may be applied to any [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishops_in_the_Catholic_Church bishop], it was implied that Sulyvahn holds the highest possible position in the Church of Irithyll.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Sulyvahn was a humanoid creature born and raised in the Painted World of Ariandel. Despite his isolation from the outside world, he demonstrated incredible intelligence and talent for sorcery as a young man; he created new frost-based sorceries, using the cold climate of his home to strengthen weapons or form clouds of freezing mist. At some point Sulyvahn became dissatisfied with living inside the Painted World, as he had not experienced the loss or despair of those who ended up there to seek refuge after having lost everything else, and decided to abandon it, leaving behind the sorceries he developed to seek knowledge and experiences in the outside world.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn consolidated his rule of the church and the city, wielding in his right hand the ceremonial Profaned Greatsword infused with the power of the dark Profaned Flame that had fueled his ambitions and in his left hand the ceremonial Greatsword of Judgment, a symbol of his authority as Gwyndolin's judge, but actually infused with moon magic very close to dark sorcery. The two swords together was not only a representation of the violent rule of Sulyvahn but also an avowal of the Pontiff's dark roots. In fact, the Pontiff spread the practice of sorcery even among the highest ranks of his clergy and his knights and began to carry out various experiments on darkness. The humans who worked on the city were enslaved and reduced to conditions of extreme misery; their Dark Soul would manifest outside their ghostly bodies as monstrous beasts with human faces, wandering the streets. Meanwhile, in the prisons, Sulyvahn tried to transform people into pale dragons, but only managed to produce

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: With Pontiff Sulyvahn's rise to power in Irithyll, as well as his complete domination of the Way of White faith within the city, Aldrich's depraved habit became likely to draw unwanted attention to the Pontiff's new "holy" regime. In response, Pontiff Sulyvahn seems to have exiled Aldrich to the Cathedral of the Deep, which specialized in rituals of purification from "stagnant darkness", in hopes that the sacred and serene waters of the Cathedral would contain Aldrich's dark habit. The Pontiff also gave one of his small dolls to Aldrich, in the event that he recovered to a point where he could return home.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Despite having lost the source of his religious and political power, Sulyvahn, still wearing his torn robes from the battle, remained in the city's cathedral. The Pontiff set about bringing his knights back to life through necromancy, and had them patrol lower Irithyll as frigid spirits. In addition, his beasts regained control over access to the city and cornered Archdeacon McDonnell, who was leading Aldrich's legion, into the Water Reserve, implying his resolve to bring the city back under his control while Aldrich was still busy digesting Gwyndolin.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the manor at the outskirts of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley was the house that was granted to Sulyvahn when he was accepted into the society of the nobles. The original description of the bonfire is "Abandoned House on the Outskirts of the City” (街はずれの廃屋)", implying that the Manor was built on the edge of the city as its inhabitant was not equal to the other nobles of divine origins, and that it had become abandoned by the time that Sulyvahn would have ascended to Pontiff. Furthermore, the "Distant Manor" bonfire is en route to the Irithyll Dungeon and consequently the Profaned Capital, where Sulyvahn would find the Profaned Flame below Irithyll, making the access under his house a logical point along his discovery. Curiously, the manor is also the place where the city's sewage system dumped its waste.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn would also craft dark eye rings for his Boreal Outrider Knights, an order of knights who were sent away to serve in foreign campaigns as exiles. The Pontiff exploited the Outriders through these rings that would boost their attacks or recover their health as long as their fighting persisted; the process would lead to the Outrider Knights turning into raving, mindless warriors and guards. The end result ensured the unquestioning, unwavering obedience of the ferocious Outrider Knights to the Pontiff. The knights who peered inside the black orbs would be lured into visions of endless deadly battles and go insane, transformed into frenzied beasts. However, the effect of the rings, whose black eyes constantly hound the knights, continues over time, first fusing their armor with their own hide and then devolving them into beasts under the complete control of the Pontiff. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

title: Pontiff Knight
snippet: When Pontiff Sulyvahn plotted to control Irithyll, he corrupted their leaders thanks to the unquenchable Profaned Flame that he found in the ruins of the Profaned Capital. After turning the captains of the army of Irithyll into sorcerers in his service, Sulyvahn also influenced the knights they led, gifting them golden crowns as they helped him seize power. After he took power, the knights would serve as Sulyvahn's watchful eyes and punitive blades. When Aldrich and his Deacons attacked Irithyll, the Pontiff Knights were all slain, and now they are frigid spirits brought back to life by the Pontiff's necromancy. Their swords are now gnawed by the insects of the deep spawned by the Evangelists, and the knights continuously spit dark souls as their bodies were hit and filled by the sorceries of the deacons.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : Sulyvahn is a tall humanoid clothed in torn ceremonial robes, with nothing on his feet. He wears a crown and is adorned with a necklace of his eye rings. His skin is pale and seems to be decayed and covered in large cracks. His face is covered in dark roots; when he is brought to half of his life, masses of similar roots and branches emerge from his back, akin to wings.

Sulyvahn wields two greatswords: the Profaned Ultra Greatsword in his right hand and the Greatsword of Judgment in his left. When the Ashen One enters the church, Sulyvahn is standing still with his two swords; when approached, his swords start to glow and he advances towards the player before quickly charging with an overhead slash.

During the fight, Sulyvahn can be heard grunting and growling in a deep, distorted voice.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Despite his coup and the partial schism that saw the Church of Carim establish itself as the alternative political and religious center of the Way of White, Sulyvahn continued to remain an ally of Lothric, donating the Gargoyles he found in the Profaned Capital to the kingdom and allowing their knights and scholars into Irithyll. This powerful alliance allowed the Pontiff to retain international legitimacy and political leverage to strengthen his position and keep other human realms and high members of the clergy faithful to his faction.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn is extremely susceptible to parrying, each riposte dealing upwards of 1000 damage. A couple of his moves can be easily exploited as the swings of his flaming sword are usually telegraphed and can be predicted. Utilizing parry and riposte throughout the battle can end the fight quickly, leaving him close to death just as he begins to summon the phantom.

An easier method that forgoes parries (and even rolling) is to simply circle around him clockwise while raising a shield that offers 100% physical absorption. Circling left (Sulyvahn's right) will avoid almost every attack and allow you time to land one or two hits after most of his attack patterns. When he begins to summon a phantom, start attacking immediately to kill the phantom as quick as possible and resume circling clockwise. Since this strategy allows you to steadily attack throughout the fight, it will typically end before he tries to summon another one.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn continued to climb the ranks of the Way of White's clergy and increase his influence until, at one point, Gwyndolin was "stricken by illness" and was forced into retiring from the government of the city, leaving command of the Blades of the Darkmoon to his younger sister Yorshka. The sorcerer took advantage of the situation and proclaimed himself "Pontiff", the legitimate representative of the god, who would act as the ad interim ruler over the realm of Irithyll and as head of the Church. The Silver Knights, still faithful to Gwyndolin, and the Blades of the Darkmoon serving Yorshka could have acted against his wrongful proclamation; therefore Sulyvahn preemptively imprisoned the god in the old cathedral of Anor Londo and his sister on the tower of her church, creating a stalemate in which neither the Silver Knights nor the Blades of the Darkmoon could act, afraid of seeing their captive leaders executed.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Having gained power in Irithyll, Sulyvahn set about cleansing the city of potential enemies, exiling or killing the Blades of the Darkmoon until there were no more knights in the order, eliminating the Painting Guardians, and even turning the Giants who worked in the city into slaves. The Pontiff would also build an immense dungeon underground near the Profaned Capital, employing its survivors as cruel jailers in his service, and building prisons for humans around the oldest cell of a giant. In addition, Sulyvahn erected a magic barrier around Irithyll to prevent anyone from entering or leaving without his permission, giving special dolls to his most valued subjects to move through it freely, an artifact which reminded them ceaselessly that their "home" would always be the Boreal Valley. title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: During the fight, it is advised to not extend one's attacks for more than two swings as you would need your stamina to dodge or absorb Pontiff's aggressive retaliation. Sulyvahn's attacks can be difficult to avoid due to varying delays, rapidly chaining combos and the large distances that they can cover. Watch out for the downward strike and impaling slide attacks that he performs - they are telegraphed and have long recovery time, giving you time to strike back or heal up.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: With great foresight and manipulation, Sulyvahn began his rise to power within Irithyll: the sorcerer used the Profaned Flame to enthrall the city's holy knights, corrupting their hearts with the unquenchable version of the Fire they venerated. His influence expanded also to the troops they commanded who became Sulyvahn's personal knights, reporting directly to him, acting as his watchful eyes first and as his designated killers second, effectively becoming his private militia and secret police. Those who were once holy knights became "fire witches" who carried the Profaned Flame of Sulyvahn on Immolation Tinders, also catalysts for the sorcery once so abhorred by the clergy, while the swords of the soldiers they led were imbued with the frost magic of their leader.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Once you enter through the fog gate, be cautious as you approach Pontiff as he will likely leap at you with his sword from a distance. With good timing, this attack can be parried, immediately giving you the upper hand.

As most of his combos are mid or mid-long range, two-handed shield-less builds should roll behind him because the only attacks that hit behind his back are turning pirouette attacks (or jump and plunge attacks in the second phase) that are easier to dodge than his multi-hit combos. Pontiff also overcommits to some attacks and can be combo-locked, giving a player the chance to deal free damage from behind. He will turn around but his turn is slow enough that a player can reposition behind his back. If Pontiff moves to mid-range, close the distance from the side and reposition behind his back.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: One day, when Sulyvahn was still young, he unearthed the Profaned Capital underneath the outskirts of Irithyll; he also discovered in the ruins of the city the Profaned Flame. It was a "cold" flame, found preserved in icy remains; it was an unfading, everlasting flame, and one that held within it the Dark of humanity. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
There is a statue in the High Wall of Lothric that resembles Sulyvahn, in the square patrolled by the Winged Knight. It depicts a barefooted man in the Robe of Prayer wielding the Profaned Greatsword and wearing bracelets, both of which are on the right wrist, similar to Sulyvahn's own bracelets.
**It is although more likely that the statue is an example of propaganda through symbolism, where the young Prince Lothric, embodiment of the hope of all realms, would carry on the legacy of the Linking of the Fire armed with the Pontiff's Sword, symbol of the support of the Church, strength of Faith and power of the Fire.
The Pontiff seems to lack a face, and the front of his head is instead covered in what looks like roots. Removing his armor and the root-like formations shows a completely featureless face.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
With Pontiff Sulyvahn relinquishing Gwyndolin, the Saint of the Deep was triumphant, taking up residence in the old Cathedral and beginning to feast on the old god. He would fall into a deep slumber in the process of consuming Gwyndolin, during which he would dream and perceive the form of a young, pale girl in hiding. The Aldrich Faithful guarded the old Cathedral to ward off any intrusion on Aldrich's slumber, with the ancient Silver Knights unwittingly aiding the consumption of their former master.

When the Ashen One seeking the Lords of Cinder arrives at Irithyll to slay Aldrich in their quest, he awakens to defend himself, puppeteering Gwyndolin's magic and body, as well as using a miracle developed from his dreams.

title: Way of White
snippet:
The Way of White built a cathedral dedicated to the goddess Caitha and with the aim of cleansing humans from the stagnant darkness within them that was becoming an ever-increasing problem, using the "sacred and peaceful" body of water on which the structure was built to contain all the remnants from its cleansing rituals and even sent three archdeacons to manage it.

At a certain point, the king of the gods Gwyndolin was struck by an "illness" and Sulyvahn took advantage of it, locking the god in the old abandoned cathedral of Anor Londo and proclaiming himself "Pontiff", thus assuming command of the Way of White. This caused a schism within the Way of White, as the Church of Carim and its Archbishop did not recognize Sulyvahn's authority, separating themselves from the denomination of the other Archbishops who kept following the Church of Irithyll.

title: Gods
snippet:
Many Silver Knights since the Age of Ancients served Lord Gwyn and the other Old Gods of Anor Londo, well into the events of *Dark Souls III*. Their origins and species are never clearly explained.
Crossbreed Priscilla, hated by the Gods, was exiled to the Painted World of Ariamis hidden in Anor Londo. She was likely the hybrid daughter of Seath, and the mother of both Gwyndolin, with Gwyn as the father, and of Yorshka, from another father.
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: Amidst the power vacuum left by Gwyndolin's absence, Sulyvahn would take advantage of the fragile situation, declaring himself Pontiff and becoming the tyrant of Irithyll. He managed to imprison Yorshka on the tower of her own church, isolating her from the world and holding her hostage. Over time, the Darkmoon would lose every one of its followers, being integrated into the ranks of Sulyvahn's knights, killed, or exiled, leaving Yorshka as the head of a covenant with no knights and only its legacy to preserve. Yorshka would have remained alone on the tower, unable to hear from her brother, with only the chime that he had given her to console her in her solitude. Despite her imprisonment, the humans of Irithyll, now enslaved by Pontiff Sulyvahn and subjected to his experiments, would continue to pray to the goddess in secret, worshipping the sacred spears that were enchanted with a soporific spell, trying to find comfort and rest from their condition, even at the cost of hitting

The Pontiff allows the clergy to freely study sorcery and creates his own militia to guard the city. The Blades of the Darkmoon are disbanded and removed as a threat to his power
The former aristocrats and maidens of the Profaned Capital surrender to Sulyvahn, accepting to serve as jailers within Irithyll's Dungeon
Sulyvahn makes a dancer out of one of the member of the Royal Family of Anor Londo (probably a daughter of Gwynevere) as a display of power. He also casts a magic barrier around the city, and only those who carry a special doll can cross it: with this, his control over Irithyll is absolute
The Cathedral becomes corrupted by the spreading Deep, therefore Aldrich is chosen as the next Lord of Cinder to link the Fire and cleanse this raging plague

title: The Deep
snippet: themselves responsible with sealing away the horrors that rose from the Deep, to the point of needing grand stories to drive away the madness caused by these abominations. At one point, Sulyvahn sent in Archdeacon McDonnell to aid the deacons of the Cathedral, who conversely found the stagnant souls of the Deep delightful, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world".

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Vordt of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Vordt is a distant descendant of the old gods of Anor Londo. He was among the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans, who inhabit Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city built for them on the ruins of Anor Londo.

After Sulyvahn imprisoned Dark Sun Gwyndolin, proclaimed himself pontiff and assumed control of the city, Vordt was ordered to serve under the tyrant as a Boreal Outrider Knight, equivalent to being exiled. These knights, before being dispatched to foreign lands, were given the eye rings of the Pontiff, which eventually transformed them into savage, raving warriors who only knew how to serve as mindless guards, ensuring Sulyvahn's total control over them and depriving any means of desertion.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Dancer is a direct descendant of Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight. She was among the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans, who inhabit Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city built for them on the ruins of Anor Londo.

After Sulyvahn imprisoned Dark Sun Gwyndolin, proclaimed himself pontiff and assumed control of the city, he bestowed upon the Dancer a set of paired enchanted swords. A symbol of her subjugation by the tyrant, the twinblades were enchanted with dark magic in the right-hand and fire in the left, mirroring those of the Pontiff. She was then ordered to serve Sulyvahn as a "dancer".

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: At some point McDonnell was incapacitated and his body ended up in the lower levels of Irithyll, in a cistern guarded by two of Pontiff Sulyvahn's beasts, however he is still able to recognize others, as he manages Aldrich's covenant and teaches sorceries.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn ordered the Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight, equivalent to being exiled. These knights, before being dispatched to foreign lands, were given the eye rings of the Pontiff, which eventually transformed them into savage, raving warriors who only knew how to serve as mindless guards, which ensured Sulyvahn's total control over the knights and deprived them of any means of desertion.

The Dancer was sent to Lothric together with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here she positioned herself to guard the Cathedral and High Priestess Emma. Like other Outrider Knights, she would end up transformed into a frenzied beast by the rings of the Pontiff, causing her armor to be fused with her hide.

title: Gods
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.
King Oceiros, the King of Lothric who married Gwynevere. It is unknown what his original species was, but he would later become similar to a hybrid in an attempt to turn into a Dragon. He is the father of at least three of Gwynevere's children: Lorian, Lothric (named after the kingdom) and her youngest, Ocelotte, none of whom were deified; it is unclear whether or not he fathered Rosaria, the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, or Gertrude, but as Lorian was the heir to the throne, he was likely the two's oldest son, and perhaps their oldest child together.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: also be found within Lothric Castle. It's important to note that Lothric and Irithyll remained on good terms even after Sulyvahn's coup, with the Pontiff sending Gargoyles from the Profaned Capital to the Grand Archives, and Grand Archives Scholars travelling to Irithyll. The path to the Archdragon Peak is situated in Irithyll Dangeons, and many Lothric knights are bowed near the Dragon Torso Stone, implying that the knights went in pilgrimage to the Peak, and the fact that they were left untouched by the Jailers is a proof that Lothric was allied with the Pontiff.

snippet:

 description : The Aldrich Faithfuls protect Lord Aldrich from harmful ash, such as the Ashen One, and claim Human Dregs as their prizes. These may be used to rank up in the covenant for rewards.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Aldrich Faithful covenant, the player must first have cleared the area by defeating both Sulyvahn's Beasts and then proceed to Archdeacon McDonnell's remains and pray to them, at this point they may ask to join and obtain proof of the covenant.

Killing the Sulyvahn's beasts is not required to join the covenant. If one wears the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring and casts Hidden Body just as they reach the bottom of the ladder, they can sneak around the left, far wall and avoid the beasts and pray to McDonnell, thus joining.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Aldrich Faithful** is a covenant in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Like the Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful will be called upon to defend Aldrich's territory from trespassers; any player who has Host of Embers status will be subject to invasion. This area is defined as anywhere from the courtyard upon exiting Pontiff Sulyvahn's arena, up until the rotating stairway leading up to Anor Londo. Aldrich Faithful can pursue trespassers up into the cathedral itself, but will not be summoned for trespassers who have already reached the upper level bonfire.

Defeating the Host of Embers will reward all present Aldrich Faithful with Human Dregs, which can be offered to Archdeacon McDonnell to deepen their allegiance to the covenant.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - location 
 location : The Aldrich Faithful covenant can be found in the lower plane of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward and make way to the other side of the large courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering the main building on the opposite side, hit the wall on the left to reveal an illusory wall concealing the main access to the covenant.

Climb down the large ladder to reach a big, flooded hall. There are two Sulyvahn's Beasts lying in wait once reaching this area, one on the left and one further ahead on the right.

In one corner of the room lie the remains of Archdeacon McDonnell. Interacting with him allows access into the covenant.

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - description 
 description : The holy symbol of the Cathedral of the Deep, and crest of those who see beyond fire to the age of deep waters. Equip to pledge oneself to the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

The faithful ensure that Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, remains undisturbed, by taking the form of loyal spirits and hunting down those who would trespass the ruined cathedral.

Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.
